paragraph: Wyckoff is a single-family town, and the numbers there are decisive: 69 sales over six months at a median of $1,356,000, a sale-to-list ratio of 1.043, roughly 61 percent of homes selling above asking, and a median of 13 days on market. That is a real seller's market with plenty of multiple offer situations, and buyers should expect competition on the good ones. The typical sale is a four-bedroom colonial with two full baths, with ranches and split-levels making up most of the rest. Sales ran from $550,000 to $3,350,000, so the median is the number to anchor on. The monthly series tracks the normal seasonal arc almost exactly: volume built from 10 closings in February to 19 in June and 20 in July, with the median climbing to $1,425,000 in June and holding essentially flat at $1,397,500 in July. If Wyckoff follows the usual pattern, expect volume to taper modestly through fall and thin out in deep winter. Townhouses are a small piece here, 5 sales at a median of $952,800, too few to read a trend from, though all five moved quickly. If you're weighing the two, the deciding factor isn't market heat. It's whether you want the space and grounds of a single-family or the low-maintenance setup of a townhouse.
